item.description: AMD unveiled its Ryzen AI Max PRO 400 processors at a Beijing media event on September 10, alongside partners like Flowy and Nova showing Mini PCs, compact workstations, laptops and AI NAS built on the platform. The chip offers up to 128GB of unified memory, 96GB of which can be allocated as VRAM, letting local LLMs, long-context RAG and multi-agent workflows run across CPU, GPU and NPU. It targets developers weighing on-device agent deployment.

item.title: [infoq] AI 有了“工号”，数据平台长出了手：我在 Snowflake World Tour 看到的三个变化
item.description: Writing up Snowflake World Tour Shanghai, the author draws three takeaways from global product president Christian Kleinerman's keynote: agents now get Agent Identity and Policy, effectively an employee ID capping what they can read, write, move and spend; data platforms are starting to take action rather than just answer queries; and Snowflake is embracing open source. Aimed at data and AI practitioners tracking enterprise agent adoption.

item.title: [infoq] AI Coding 的下一步不是写得更快，而是可验收：蚂蚁数科 Harness 工程实践
item.description: At AICon, Ant Digital Technologies expert Wei Changzheng described a "Harness" engineering approach: a 400k-line Rust project had Harness built into its workflow from day one, while a 600k-line legacy C++ project first rebuilt its source of truth and quality gates before agents were allowed to upgrade the repo, cutting defect rates from over 20% to single digits. His argument: verifiability, not speed, is AI coding's next step.

item.title: [infoq] 刘震云对话马毅：人写不出来、想不到的作品，AI 模仿不了｜附完整对话
item.description: At a roundtable at the Inclusion Bund Conference in Shanghai on September 10, novelist Liu Zhenyun and Ma Yi, dean of HKU's School of Computing and Data Science, debated what stays uniquely human as AI advances. Liu said 95% of videos using his likeness are fake, yet AI cannot imitate works he hasn't written; Ma argued LLMs grasp only humanity's shared knowledge, not individual character, and that education should teach students to amplify their own skills with AI.

Ant's AI payments head Zhu Lin expects natural new-interaction payments to top 50% within five years, with smart-device payments up tenfold.

item.title: [infoq] 怒斥加密货币是旁氏骗局、放弃80%就业机会也不用 AI 写代码！Kotlin“J神”：AI 会让工程师变成可替换的齿轮
item.description: Jake Wharton, a well-known Android and Kotlin open source developer, has listed nine criteria for his next job, starting with a refusal to join AI companies, work on AI-centric products, or accept mandatory AI tooling — a rule he estimates rules out roughly 80% of employers. He says he has never used an AI agent to write code, arguing AI can handle repetitive work but that generating code beyond a developer's ability to understand and maintain is the most irresponsible use.

item.description: Wang Zefeng, a stability engineer at Kuaishou, presented the company's 'Conan AI' work at AICon Shanghai: deterministic steps go to code, probabilistic reasoning to models, with expert experience captured as Skills and bad cases driving iteration. The system has reached nearly 60% adoption among Kuaishou's front-end R&D staff, with about 50% full adoption of its root-cause analyses, and located a pure system-stack Use-After-Free issue behind a HarmonyOS C++ crash in roughly 10 minutes.

It installs via `npx @exoticknight/red` and is aimed at teams that want AI to support long-running iteration rather than one-off code generation.

item.description: A developer shipped a WeChat mini-game, "Happy Link-Up", spending about two months of spare time and roughly $6 (WeChat certification plus Tencent Cloud OSS). The stack is pixi.js@6, matter-js, Vite and Supabase, with Claude Code writing the code and gpt, gemini and Doubao generating art. The write-up lists 19 mini-game pitfalls, a reusable Claude Code prompt workflow and the full cost breakdown, useful for solo devs building with AI.

item.description: CloddsBot is an open-source trading agent that runs autonomously across 1000+ markets — Polymarket, Kalshi, Binance, Hyperliquid, Solana DEXs and five EVM chains — scanning for edge, executing orders instantly and managing risk. It's written in TypeScript (Node 22+), ships 121+ skills under the MIT license, and was built for the Colosseum Agent Hackathon.

item.title: [juejin] 白嫖DeepSeek V4 Pro！免费无限用，还能接入Claude-Code
item.description: This tutorial shows a five-step path to DeepSeek V4 Pro's free tier: sign up on ZenMux, create an API key restricted to deepseek-v4-flash-free and deepseek-v4-pro-free, and connect it locally via cc-switch or Cherry Studio for use in Claude-Code. A sample response in the post says it is not actually DeepSeek-v4, so verify the real model and quota yourself.

item.title: [github_trending] asgeirtj/system_prompts_leaks
item.description: This repo collects verbatim system prompts that chatbots such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok receive before a user's first message, spanning models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI. Its files have been used by The Washington Post for an interactive story and by CEPS' AI World for a live dashboard, making it a reference for developers studying how these products constrain model behavior.

item.title: [github_trending] p1neappleXpress/OpenFlux
item.description: OpenFlux describes itself as a network stack research tool offering a TCP tunnel with pluggable transports, with client downloads listed for platforms including Android. The README is almost entirely a disclaimer: the project is non-commercial, has no paid features, and the author does not encourage using it to bypass platform restrictions — beyond that, the linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [juejin] DeepSeek Harness 值得安装的 15 款插件
item.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is gaining traction and its plugin ecosystem is expanding rapidly; this article highlights 15 plugins worth installing. Developers already using DSH and wanting to extend their workflow should find it a useful starting point.

item.title: [juejin] AI写长篇小说为什么30章必崩
item.description: The post uses a ChatGPT novel as an example: early chapters are vivid and tight, but around chapter 30 continuity collapses—a heroine's sister changes name and a setup from chapter 5 is forgotten. It then explains why this failure happens in long-form AI writing and outlines an engineering-oriented fix, making it relevant for developers and authors producing long texts with LLMs.

item.title: [juejin] 这个本地模型，让我 token 自由了
item.description: The post looks at Qwen3.8-27B, a local model that brings flagship-level agent capability to a personal machine without paying API fees. The author is upfront about the trade-offs: inference speed, memory footprint and long-task experience remain real barriers. It suits developers willing to run local inference who can live with slower responses.

item.title: [github_trending] jihe520/MathModelAgent
item.description: MathModelAgent is an agent built for mathematical modeling that automates the modeling workflow and produces a paper ready to submit. Its recommended desktop build bundles Claude Code and the full set of MathModelAgent skills, so no Python, Node.js or Redis setup is needed — just a model API key; macOS builds are signed and notarized while Windows ones are not.

item.title: [github_trending] Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps
item.description: awesome-llm-apps is a curated GitHub repo of more than 100 open-source AI agents, agent skills and RAG apps, released under Apache-2.0 and compatible with Claude, Gemini, GPT, DeepSeek, Llama and Qwen. Each template is hand-built and tested end-to-end, with step-by-step tutorials on Unwind AI, so developers can clone and ship instead of writing boilerplate from scratch.

item.title: [github_trending] armory3d/armorpaint
item.description: ArmorPaint is a 3D PBR texture painting tool whose GitHub repository is aimed at developers; the maintainers note the code here may not be stable, and ready-made binaries are sold to fund the project. Building from source requires a platform toolchain — Visual Studio with clang tools on Windows, clang and dependencies on Linux, Xcode for macOS/iOS, Android Studio for Android.

item.title: [github_trending] Sonarr/Sonarr
item.description: Sonarr is a PVR for Usenet and BitTorrent users that watches multiple RSS feeds for new episodes of your shows, then grabs, sorts and renames them, and can automatically upgrade already-downloaded files when a better-quality release appears. The project ships a wiki and API docs alongside forum and Discord support, while GitHub Issues is reserved for bugs and feature requests.

item.title: [github_trending] nab138/iloader
item.description: iloader is a user-friendly sideloading tool that installs SideStore and other apps and imports your pairing file without manual fuss; its builds run through GitHub Actions. The project states that the repository and iloader.app are the only official download sources, alongside unofficial Homebrew, AUR and Fedora COPR packages. It targets people who sideload onto iOS devices but prefer a GUI to a command line.
